overall_summary: Recent 7-day performance data clearly shows that extreme space scenarios, speculative 'What If' planetary physics, and high-value astronomical anomalies ('Liquid Diamond Planet', 'Venus Day vs Year', 'Planet Darker Than Coal') dominate both view counts and engagement (likes/comments per view). Videos featuring speculative spatial hazards outperform simple static facts. Conversely, older psychological tricks and minor biological facts suffer from low velocity and weak engagement.

winning_patterns.evidence: Videos like 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' (1,024 views) and 'What If You Fell Into the Darkest Planet?' (825 views) achieve top-tier view velocity and strong like ratios.
winning_patterns.action: Double down on high-stakes hypothetical space immersion hooks that force the viewer to mentally visualize extreme physical environments.

winning_patterns.evidence: 'The Planet Darker Than Coal: TrES-2b' (1,026 views) and 'Venus Has a Day Longer Than Its Year' (722 views) generated significant organic engagement within days of release.
winning_patterns.action: Focus on lesser-known, bizarre exoplanets and cosmic phenomena with counterintuitive numerical facts.

weak_patterns.evidence: 'The Psychological Trick to Stop Songs Stuck in Your Head' (71 views) and 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' (53 views) show stagnant view velocity compared to space content.
weak_patterns.action: Deprioritize psychological life-hacks and pivot those resources toward hard-hitting physics and space mysteries.

weak_patterns.evidence: Simple creature facts like 'Octopuses Have THREE Hearts' received moderate initial traction but low overall engagement compared to planetary destruction scenarios.
weak_patterns.action: Elevate animal content into cinematic survival or extreme evolutionary anomalies rather than basic static listicle facts.
